content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: Authors proposed a new pipeline which combined TDA and a 3-layer neural networks to classify cancer types based on TCGA. More specifically, authors evaluated the pipeline with respect to three pairwise classification tasks: LUAD-vs-COAD-READ, COAD-READ-vs-BRCA and LUAD-vs-BRCA. Authors highlighted the novelty of the pipeline by performing an ablation test which removed the all the preprocessing modules including the TDA module.�
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
(-) Classification of the gene expression data using deep learning is not far from solved as stated in the introduction section. I includ one related manuscript [1] for reference, which achieved a high classification accuracy leveraging a simple KNN classification model with a pre-selection step using genetic algorithms.

(-) Authors stated that the non-TDA baseline was a MLP classifier directly building upon the raw gene expression data. It’s not clear whether authors filtered the raw gene expression based on differential analysis or not. Authors didn’t include any other baseline classification methods for comparison either.

(-) It’s unclear how much improvement is contributed by the TDA representations. Authors should perform additional ablation tests by eliminating preprocessing steps, especially the differential analysis step, and keeping the TDA embedding step. 

1.	Li, Yuanyuan, et al. "A comprehensive genomic pan-cancer classification using The Cancer Genome Atlas gene expression data." BMC genomics 18.1 (2017): 1-13.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The research problem of predicting cancer phenotype was not properly motivated, and authors didn’t have a good knowledge of this field. The evaluation procedure was not clear (see “Strength and weakness”), and the novelty of the proposed pipeline was very limited. Overall, the manuscript is not ready yet to be presented in its current form.�
content.summary_of_the_review: This manuscript is not of interest to the general ML community (see comments above). Also authors disclosed their identities which violates the double-blind policy of ICLR2023.�
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The manuscript entitled “Topological Data Analysis-Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Cancer Phenotypes” applies the Persistent Diagram measurement, which aims to characterize the topological relationship among data points, to the gene expression data for phenotype prediction.
content.strength_and_weaknesses: Weakness: The manuscript did not provide sufficient evidence that the proposed method would be superior in predicting gene phenotypes and its generalizability when used at a new site/task. Specifically, the author did not explain the “Non-TDA” methods used in Tables 1, 2, and 3, which is important as there has been extensive research linking gene expression and its phenotypes. It is even more curious that the “Non-TDA” methods achieved <50% Accuracy in binary classification tasks, indicating they were not correctly implemented.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea of using topological representations and graph theory-derived measurements in analyzing genetic data has been extensively investigated in the past decade. The key methods used in this work, the Persistent Diagram and the corresponding Persistent Landscapes / Persistent Images representations, were developed by earlier works. For reproducibility, although the source code is not provided in the manuscript, as it uses public data as model input and off-the-shelf R packages for the analysis, this work should be reproducible with minimum effort.
content.summary_of_the_review: A single-site experiment utilizing topological representations for supervised binary phenotype prediction from gene expression data. The model lacks novelty and sufficient results to support its generalizability and robustness.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

display_title: Official Review of Paper4685 by Reviewer 7K87

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: An application paper, where a classical topological technique (Persistence Homology PH analysis) was used on a single gene expression dataset (TCGA), also for a classical application - cancer phenotype prediction. Gene pre-selection was performed in order to reduce the computational time of processing persistence diagrams.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
It is interesting to see applications of TDA in genetics and medicine, in general. More and more papers have been published in this field over the past 5 years. The paper is accurately written, with no grammar or lexical mistakes, and hence easily readable. However, on the methodological level, there are several deficiencies. 
1. 50 epochs trained on a shallow MLP is kind of expected to produce poor results, with an accuracy of 46.15. This obviously can't be treated as a benchmark. In the following comprehensive review (https://genomemedicine.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13073-021-00968-x), one can see that mostly either CNN or ensemble models were used. In the case of MLP, mostly the last layer of MLP is used with Cox Regression analysis for prediction tasks, including on transcriptome datasets. And the results achieved are not that far. 
2. Assuming that with Persistence Homology authors expected to catch underlying topology at different scales, the following is missing. Why there should be any clear topology worth exploring? Why Persistence Landscapes (PL) and Images (PI) were not displayed and interpreted? In the medical domain where the interpretability of a result is no less important than the result itself, TDA offers the exact advantage of providing that. I think anyone who reads the paper would expect that in the first place, namely, what kind of PLs and PIs the model is learning and basing its prediction upon, clearly illustrated and interpreted.
3. the number of predicted cancer phenotypes is limited (only 3, LUAD, BRCA and COAD-READ). Nothing was said about whether the results can be generalized to other cancer phenotypes.
4. about the dataset: authors used TCGA, a total of 160 LUAD, 133 BRCA and 158 COAD-READ samples, for each dataset 19958 protein-coding genes were selected, removing non-coding RNAs. This dataset might be augmented by merging other open-source datasets too, such as ICGC, GEO, EGPA, and METABRIC. In that case, with more epochs and right preprocessing maybe, even with MLP one can potentially achieve similar results.
6. Looking at the references, it feels like the most interesting references were not there. For example, what were the previous attempts at doing predictions on transcriptome datasets, using DL/ML models. What gave authors the motivation to try TDA.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- the paper is clearly written and easily readable. 
- the quality is neither poor, nor at the top. Many additions and corrections must be made to boost the quality to the top. 
- there is a novelty in the ideological/methodological sense, but not in a sense of beating the state-of-the-art benchmark results. Furthermore, the above-mentioned weaknesses must be addressed in order to illustrate the novelty in the maximum potential, otherwise, at the moment it is not quite clear why the results are worth attention. 
- to generate Persistence diagrams is computationally expensive, which is a pitfall of PH analysis and it should be mentioned, especially for those who are planning to replicate results for a much larger dataset. But unfortunately, the authors didn't make the code open-source, hence no one can replicate it exactly how they did. Nevertheless, it's straightforward to set up an environment for PD processing and MLP, and the dataset is open source, so it's not a big loss.

Although persistence diagrams are the classical TDA approach, it should be mentioned in future works what other TDA techniques could be used to extract more features, as well as how TDA can be combined with a more sophisticated ML model (this is a typical approach taken in the field).
content.summary_of_the_review: in my opinion, in the current state the paper will be rejected by ICLR, since the above-mentioned weaknesses are very vivid and must be addressed.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.details_of_ethics_concerns: Author names must be invisible to reviewers. I can see the authors and their affiliations, which naturally introduces bias in reviewers' judgments.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper authors propose a topological data analysis (TDA) approach to pre-select genes for disease association. They use multiple topological representations  for classifying three cancer phenotypes. 
Instead of using DL on raw data they use topological features to predict the cancer type. They use two topological representations so called persistent landscapes (PL) and persistent images (PI). Their aim of applying Deep learning (DL) on these topological representations instead of using raw data is to get ride of extreme noise in Gene expression data and identifying subtle signals embedded in the data for the classification of cancer types.
As a baseline they use a  non-TDA approach and their experimental results show that applying DL on topological representations improve prediction of cancer types in terms of reported evaluation metrics including ACC, F1, TPR and Precision.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
The proposed approach seems really effective in addressing the underlying problem. 

Weaknesses:
1- The paper was not written in the ICLR style.
2- The paper includes the name of the authors that is against the double blind review process of ICLR.
3- In introduction part, authors provide backgrounds on Persistent Homology and  Topological Representations in Sections 1.2 and 1.3. Some required concepts to describe their methods such as  persistent landscapes and persistent Images are not defined properly. 
4- In method part, in section 2.2 they describe the TDA implementation.  They did not describe the notations and concepts that they use to describe their methods properly. For example in  page 3 they write:

The distance correlation matrix was determined from X train by calculating all pairwise distances between genes (Xs,i; Xs,j) F ∈ [0, 1]. But they did not say what is F?
Or in the same page, they mention:
To construct Mi,j differential gene expression analysis was used to identify significantly up- and down-regulated genes. But they never described what is M_ij. 
The same problem exist in the last paragraph of section 2.2. 

5- The computational complexity of the proposed approach was not explained.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1- In terms of novelty, applying DL on features extracted using TDA seems really effective in terms of caner prediction.

2- In terms of Clarity and quality, the method is heavily relied on knowledge about topology and the required concepts were not described properly.  

3- The notations were poorly chosen. And there are some used notations and symbols that were not described.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method seems really effective for the practitioners in the field. However the paper was not written in a proper way. Both background and method parts can be described in a more structured way by choosing consistent notations.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
